title: Everywhere All at Once: Co-Location Attacks on Public Cloud FaaS
problem: Achieving physical host co-location between attacker and victim in public cloud FaaS environments is challenging due to widespread VPC adoption, large data center sizes, and dynamic function instance placement with limited attacker control.
motivation: Microarchitectural side-channel attacks require co-location to exploit shared hardware resources, posing significant threats to cloud-hosted applications.
method: The attacker exploits how the cloud platform schedules functions and allocates resources to place their own functions on the same physical machine as a target victim—bypassing the VPC isolation that should keep them separate. Once co-located, both functions share the CPU cache (fast memory that multiple processes access). The attacker observes timing patterns in this shared cache, using them as a side-channel (an indirect way to leak information) to figure out what sensitive data the victim function is processing.
key_novelty: This is the first practical demonstration that an attacker can force their function onto the same physical machine as a victim function in public cloud FaaS platforms, defeating both VPC isolation and dynamic instance placement.
contributions: Demonstrates practical co-location attack methods for FaaS environments
Reveals scheduling vulnerabilities that enable attacker-victim co-location
Shows microarchitectural side-channel exploitation in dynamic cloud settings
Exposes FaaS security gaps despite VPC-based isolation mechanisms
